newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK SOFTER ON KEY UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK SOFTER ON KEY UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed the week on Friday easier against most hard currencies, foreign exchange dealers said.

"The market was very dull until sometime this afternoon when people started selling (U.S. dollars). Probably one or two guys had picked up some tobacco money," one dealer commented, saying this saw the local currency appreciate by a cent from its morning levels.
"But then the central bank came into the market buying and we went back to our opening levels," he added.

Dealers say the Reserve Bank has been very active in the market in recent weeks, mopping up any surplus foreign currency around to keep the local dollar down, given the latest rise in annual inflation to 22.4 percent from 19.9 percent.

"We've been seeing a very strong intervention policy by the Reserve Bank. They're tightly monitoring the Zimbabwe dollar to make sure it doesn't appreciate from these current levels," one dealer said on Friday.
The local unit finished the day at 11.2950/3050 from 11.2900/3000 overnight and at 18.5300/5500 from 18.5100/5300 against sterling.
It was at 6.6500/6700 from Thursday's 6.6300/6500 versus the mark but gained a cent to 2.5200/5400 from 2.5300/5500 against South Africa's rand.
